newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, market waits for elections.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, market waits for elections.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.46 percent on Thursday and traders said they expect the market to drift sideways until the general elections on November 10.

"Shares fell today due to a lack of active participation. Focus has shifted to shares of newly privatised firms that are expected to be listed soon. Otherwise, no major changes are expected before the elections," said Saso Cacic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 14.13 points to 954.81.
* 13 shares fell and two rose, while eight were untraded.
* Total turnover fell to 53 million tolars from 62.5 million.
* Bank SKB was the most actively traded, falling 5.15 percent to 24,133 tolars on volume of 497 shares for total turnover of 11.9 million tolars.
* Drug wholesaler Salus was the leading decliner, falling 7.08 percent to 13,582 tolars on volume of 640 shares for total turnover of 8.7 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the biggest gainer, firming 2.94 percent to 10,500 tolars on volume of 200 shares for total turnover of 2.1 million tolars.
